cases.name: UN: August 2026 civilian casualties
cases.disposition: At least 372 killed and 2,349 injured in August 2026 per OHCHR snapshot
cases.fact: OHCHR documented civilian harm across Ukraine and warned that published figures represent verified minimums.
cases.limits: Monthly totals can be revised; do not compare incompatible report vintages or infer a live count.

cases.name: UN: October civilian-protection concern
cases.disposition: UN human rights chief condemned deadly attacks and highlighted outages and risks to civilians.
cases.fact: Documented public concern for civilians throughout Ukraine, including deaths from Russian strikes and allegations of civilian harm in Russian-controlled areas or Russia.
cases.limits: Some incident numbers are attributed to local authorities pending independent verification.

cases.name: DoD: civilian-harm policy
cases.disposition: DoDI 3000.17 framework for civilian-harm mitigation and response.
cases.fact: U.S. DoD described institutional requirements to mitigate and assess civilian harm during U.S. military operations.
cases.limits: Does not grant this application official DoD authority or apply to all foreign military actions unchanged.

cases.name: DOJ: unlawful electronics procurement case
cases.disposition: Andrey Shevlyakov pleaded guilty to export violations.
cases.fact: Specific illicit supply-chain case illustrates why distributor knowledge, manufacturer origin and criminal law must be separated.
cases.limits: A conviction for a scheme is not proof every branded component maker knowingly supported illicit transfers.

actions.owner: Civilian-harm research team / voluntary NGO partners
actions.ask: Publish a dated, sourced civilian-impact brief and correct evident data errors.
actions.mechanism: Shared factual baseline for diplomacy and humanitarian prioritization.
actions.gate: Public-source only; protect survivor privacy and verification standards.
actions.measure: Cited corrections and independently confirmed protection gaps.
actions.stop: Remove claims when primary evidence fails; do not publish sensitive locations.
actions.cost: Low for desk research; uncertain staffing.

actions.owner: DoD public liaison / legal-policy staff, subject to authorization
actions.ask: Audit existing public civilian-harm procedures and create an accountable referral map.
actions.mechanism: Direct problems to proper government or humanitarian mechanisms.
actions.gate: DoD policy approval; do not pretend official intake.
actions.measure: Mandates documented and channels verified.
actions.stop: Stop if a proposed referral compromises neutrality or exposes personal data.

actions.owner: U.S. departments and licensed contractors
actions.ask: Review existing end-use and supplier integrity controls for authorized defense assistance.
actions.mechanism: Discourage unlawful diversion without obstructing legitimate defense.
actions.gate: Acquisition counsel, legal scope, exporter protections.
actions.measure: Documented audit completion and verified discrepancies resolved.
actions.stop: Suspend speculative referrals; preserve due process.

actions.owner: Civil defense / authorized infrastructure partners
actions.ask: Coordinate non-sensitive energy, water and medical restoration gaps with Ukrainian consent.
actions.mechanism: Reduce harm and the pressure created by infrastructure attacks.
actions.gate: Host consent, humanitarian independence and deconfliction requirements.
actions.measure: Restored service days, verified civilian access, outage duration.
actions.stop: Pause when shared data could reveal critical vulnerabilities.

actions.owner: Diplomats with UN/OSCE consultation; states must consent
actions.ask: Design a pilot reciprocal energy and civilian-infrastructure non-attack arrangement.
actions.mechanism: A bounded, measurable confidence-building step.
actions.gate: Explicit parties’ acceptance; no implied military enforcement mandate.
actions.measure: Independent incident reviews and service interruptions.
actions.stop: No unilateral sanctions relief before verified response.

actions.owner: Independent monitoring body authorized by parties
actions.ask: Establish protected incident-intake and adjudication rules for a limited truce.
actions.mechanism: Separate deliberate violations, misidentification, accidents and disputed allegations.
actions.gate: Access, mandate, security, confidentiality, data standards.
actions.measure: Time to acknowledge and adjudicate incidents; reversals and corrections.
actions.stop: Withhold disputed findings pending verification.

actions.owner: Governments / authorized guarantors / humanitarian stakeholders
actions.ask: Develop monitored general ceasefire with security safeguards and reciprocal conditionality.
actions.mechanism: Make renewed aggression less attractive and breaches observable.
actions.gate: Mutual consent, legal review, ceasefire scope and enforcement accountability.
actions.measure: Verified compliance, humanitarian access, POW and missing-person progress.
actions.stop: Escalate violations through agreed lawful dispute process; preserve civilian access.

actions.owner: Ukraine, affected communities, donor governments, auditors
actions.ask: Support civilian-led repair, demining, accountable reconstruction and non-recurrence institutions.
actions.mechanism: Lower long-run instability, empower return and support durable security.
actions.gate: Sovereignty, public procurement audit, affected-population voice.
actions.measure: Safe return, verified cleared land, school/water uptime, grievance remedy.
actions.stop: Halt projects with unresolved displacement, corruption or environmental harm.

checks.title: Jurisdiction and mandate identified
checks.description: Confirm legal owner, civilian oversight and no assumed DoD domestic police function.

checks.title: International and domestic law reviewed
checks.description: UN Charter, IHL, human rights, procurement laws and applicable sanctions.

checks.title: Host-nation and humanitarian consent respected
checks.description: Confirm consent and do not treat neutral humanitarian organizations as intelligence sources.

checks.title: Evidence class and date recorded
checks.description: Separate verified fact, official claim, legal finding, inference, and unknown.

checks.title: Civilian-harm second-order effects assessed
checks.description: Review disruption of water, food, electricity, medical services and displacement.

checks.title: Verification and adjudication independent
checks.description: Define evidence, violations, accidents, observers and adjudicators with consent.

checks.title: Supply-chain and sanctions proportionality reviewed
checks.description: Protect lawful self-defense, humanitarian exceptions and innocent manufacturers.

checks.title: Defensive cyber only
checks.description: No access to networks, covert monitoring or intrusion; no unit positions or operational indicators.

checks.title: No protected data exposed
checks.description: Exclude classified data, restricted plans, active operations, intelligence sources and personal identifiers.

checks.title: Stop rule and fallback set
checks.description: Define a reversible contingency if facts fail, consent ends or civilian harm rises.

interventions.name: Preserve public-source evidence and manufacturer identifiers
interventions.authority: Companies, independent researchers, agencies within existing mandates
interventions.mechanism: Improve verifiable chain-of-custody and prevent premature attribution.
interventions.constraint: Retain lawful access and source rights; no blanket collection of personal information.
interventions.metric: Records with independently corroborated model, dates and provenance.

interventions.name: Refresh high-priority export-compliance training and diversion checks
interventions.authority: Exporters, distributors, compliance departments; BIS guidance
interventions.mechanism: Detect suspicious orders before shipment, preserve documentation and route to legal teams.
interventions.constraint: No automated denial based solely on nationality, geography or association.
interventions.metric: Reviewed exceptions with documented outcomes and false-positive counts.

interventions.name: Escalate substantiated financial-fraud signals
interventions.authority: Authorized financial institutions, USSS where a relevant crime nexus exists, FinCEN and prosecutors
interventions.mechanism: Address concealment, illicit payments and fraud with existing legal authorities.
interventions.constraint: SAR confidentiality, data minimization, due process; no access to banking records through this OS.
interventions.metric: Quality of lawful referrals and proportion with documented disposition.

interventions.name: Coordinate legally authorized export-control investigations
interventions.authority: Commerce BIS, HSI, FBI and DOJ as appropriate
interventions.mechanism: Connect evidence of illicit exports, actual destination and knowledge.
interventions.constraint: Proper jurisdiction, evidence admissibility and international cooperation.
interventions.metric: Verified disruptions and corrective compliance, not counts of unproven suspects.

interventions.name: Publish narrow supply-chain corrective actions
interventions.mechanism: Reduce repeated diversion by improving authorized distribution and traceability.
interventions.constraint: Avoid publication of sensitive enforcement details and civilian supply disruption.
interventions.metric: Repeat diversion incidents and measured false positives.

interventions.name: Support independently monitored diplomatic de-escalation
interventions.authority: Governments, relevant international organizations and the parties themselves
interventions.mechanism: Tie cooperation and measures to verified reductions in civilian harm and hostilities.
interventions.constraint: Ukraine’s sovereignty, consent, civilian protection and verifiable terms.
interventions.metric: Verified reduction in attacks, access to humanitarian assistance and compliance with agreements.

checks.title: Separate product maker from exporter
checks.detail: Distinguish brand, fabricator, seller, exporter, importer and eventual recipient.

checks.title: Test intent without assuming guilt
checks.detail: Legal prohibition, actor knowledge and actual transaction each need evidence.

checks.title: Apply minimization and fairness
checks.detail: No sensitive personal information or public unsupported allegations in this prototype.

checks.title: Route through authorized channels only
checks.detail: Document proposed receiving authority; do not pretend prototype files are official submissions.

checks.title: Measure corrective outcome, not arrests alone
checks.detail: Track verified compliance improvements and effects on civilian and humanitarian protection.

cases.name: August 2026 OHCHR civilian casualties
cases.disposition: At least 372 killed and 2,349 injured in Ukraine during August 2026, as documented in the September report.
cases.fact: OHCHR validated reported harm using its methodology; totals are minimums, not exhaustive or live figures.
cases.gap: Check newer monthly publication before comparing trends or claiming current rates.

cases.name: October 2026 proposed energy truce
cases.disposition: U.S. proposal publicly announced; Ukraine requested details and reported subsequent attacks; no verified implemented bilateral agreement established.
cases.fact: Statements are attributed to parties. A public proposal is not equivalent to both parties signing monitorable terms.
cases.gap: Obtain authenticated agreed text, verification mandate and independent incident findings.

cases.name: Alabuga / Generation Trading / MODAFL
cases.disposition: Treasury identified a foreign UAV procurement/production relationship with Alabuga and associated Iranian-linked entities.
cases.fact: Official designation evidence for an Iran–Russia attack-drone network; sanctions designations are not automatically criminal convictions.
cases.gap: Do not infer every supply transfer or current status in 2026 from 2024 record.

cases.name: OCCRP Geran-2 components
cases.disposition: Reporters identified 672 component shipments dated Jan 2024–Mar 2025 and multiple exporters; no evidence the named European manufacturers violated sanctions.
cases.fact: Manufacturer identification and trade flows differ from legally established knowledge of illicit end use.
cases.gap: Obtain lot trace, exporter of record, consignee, transaction history, and legal evidence of knowledge.

cases.name: Nikolay Goltsev export-control conspiracy
cases.disposition: Goltsev sentenced to 40 months for conspiring to violate export controls; electronics supplied to Russian military-linked recipients.
cases.fact: A proved unlawful procurement conspiracy; exact individual recovered chip-to-shipment chains are not universally established.
cases.gap: Link individual models to authenticated invoices only with lawful records.

actions.owner: Public-interest research team
actions.ask: Publish a versioned fact freeze separating UN civilian data, party claims and independent reporting.
actions.mechanism: Reduce decision errors caused by conflation of an announced truce with a signed one.
actions.gate: Source date, rights review, citations and public-only scope.
actions.measure: Every material claim has a source, category and last-checked date.
actions.stop: Retract or qualify disputed facts; do not release sensitive locations.
actions.cost: Low desk-research cost; staff time variable.

actions.owner: Independent analysts and domain experts
actions.ask: Draft at least three alternative explanations for negotiation deadlock and an observable refutation for each.
actions.mechanism: Make policy discussions robust against mono-causal assumptions.
actions.gate: Independent review, attribution and political neutrality.
actions.measure: Disconfirming evidence and confidence revisions publicly tracked.
actions.stop: Stop publishing unsupported motive accusations.

actions.owner: Manufacturers, distributors and export regulators within authority
actions.ask: Conduct voluntary public high-priority-component provenance review and clarify third-country diversion mechanisms.
actions.mechanism: Narrow lawful investigative leads and reduce false allegations.
actions.gate: Legal counsel, protected commercial data safeguards and due process.
actions.measure: Named model/shipper/recipient links corroborated or corrected.
actions.stop: Suspend outreach when identity or component linkage is unverified.

actions.owner: Independent research institutions; UN/OHCHR sources
actions.ask: Publish public civilian-impact and ceasefire-status baselines with transparent coverage gaps.
actions.mechanism: Support the evaluation of reciprocal civilian-protection proposals.
actions.gate: No release of protected individuals or vulnerable system detail.
actions.measure: Updated aggregate data and explicitly dated confidence classifications.
actions.stop: Withhold unverifiable incident allegations.

actions.owner: State Department, authorized negotiators and agreed neutral facilitators
actions.ask: Evaluate written sectoral energy/humanitarian truce terms before declaring success.
actions.mechanism: Verify mutual consent, scope and independent adjudication.
actions.gate: Negotiating-party consent and legal safeguards; CIA does not set policy.
actions.measure: Mutually acknowledged agreement, observer coverage and verified compliance.
actions.stop: Do not announce implementation without written terms and operational monitoring.

actions.owner: U.S./Canadian regulatory authorities and corporate compliance teams
actions.ask: Review documented sanctions-evasion networks while explicitly protecting lawful defense and humanitarian trade.
actions.mechanism: Discourage knowing illicit procurement without collective suspicion.
actions.gate: National export law, standards of proof and rights review.
actions.measure: Verified cases resolved with recorded rebuttals and legal outcomes.
actions.stop: Review if unintended civilian impacts outweigh objective gains.

actions.owner: Governments, UN-mandated or consent-based observers and local stakeholders
actions.ask: Design rights-respecting ceasefire verification, safeguards and violation appeals.
actions.mechanism: Reduce the credible-commitment gap through reciprocal observable compliance.
actions.gate: Independent mandates, lawful authority, negotiated access and non-recognition of unlawful annexation.
actions.measure: Aggregate verified incidents, time to adjudication, appeals outcomes and civilian access.
actions.stop: Suspend unsafe disclosures and revert to minimum humanitarian protection.

actions.owner: Ukraine-led reconstruction authorities, multilateral lenders and communities
actions.ask: Develop transparent rights-centered recovery and non-recurrence accountability indicators.
actions.mechanism: Make peace materially credible while retaining sovereignty and humanitarian standards.
actions.gate: Ukrainian agency, audited governance and international law.
actions.measure: Civilian infrastructure reliability, displacement outcomes, and verified non-recurrence.
actions.stop: Correct corruption or discriminatory access through independent review.

cases.name: SH Brothers / SN Electronics procurement scheme
cases.disposition: Goltsev sentenced to 40 months; others pleaded guilty or were sentenced on separate counts
cases.fact: Two Brooklyn companies procured and unlawfully shipped U.S. dual-use electronics via foreign intermediaries to Russian sanctioned defense-sector recipients. FBI, HSI and BIS/OEE cooperated.
cases.limits: The DOJ case does not establish that all original U.S. component manufacturers knowingly violated export restrictions.

cases.name: Andrey Shevlyakov electronics procurement
cases.disposition: Pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit export violations
cases.fact: A procurement network obtained sensitive electronics for Russian military and government contractors. The plea demonstrates a prosecuted unlawful procurement conspiracy.
cases.limits: The plea does not independently prove the individual shipping route for every particular recovered weapon component.

cases.name: Sergei Zharnovnikov arms-export conspiracy
cases.fact: DOJ documented unlawful export of U.S.-made firearms and ammunition through Kyrgyzstan, in violation of export licensing restrictions.
cases.limits: The case is about specific firearms and ammunition, not a general finding about every arms producer or foreign distributor.

cases.name: Vadim Yermolenko network
cases.disposition: DOJ announced guilty plea in export-control conspiracy
cases.fact: Federal prosecutors described a Russia-related defense procurement and export-control evasion conspiracy. FBI and other agencies supported the investigations.
cases.limits: Historical case; do not present the charged network as currently operating without 2026 verification.

actions.owner: Company compliance / public researcher
actions.ask: Preserve existing lawful public records and request routine compliance review.
actions.mechanism: Avoid losing provenance while protecting legitimate trade.
actions.gate: Clear public source; no person-level targeting.
actions.measure: Part numbers and dated records traced; corrections recorded.
actions.stop: Stop attribution if model mismatch or unreliable source emerges.

actions.owner: Manufacturers / distributors / BIS where appropriate
actions.ask: Reconcile returned component model, distributor allocations and licensing guidance.
actions.mechanism: Narrow the suspected diversion path and reduce false positives.
actions.gate: Authorized corporate access; legal/privacy review.
actions.measure: Shipment-model matches corroborated, plus documented nonmatches.
actions.stop: Suspend escalation when export restrictions do not apply.

actions.owner: Exporters / financial compliance teams
actions.ask: Review relevant red flags, declared end use and legal reporting obligations.
actions.mechanism: Improve KYC and address possible sanctions/export-control evasion.
actions.gate: No speculative SAR disclosure; due process and privacy.
actions.measure: Documented compliance decisions and remediation.
actions.stop: Do not infer guilt from nationality or transaction geography.

actions.owner: BIS/OEE, HSI, FBI, DOJ subject to authority
actions.ask: Evaluate documented federal nexus and decide whether authorized investigative referral is appropriate.
actions.mechanism: Build legally admissible, independently assessed cases.
actions.gate: Institution-owned investigation, not public OS action.
actions.measure: Cases with validated authority and dispositions; false-positive rate.
actions.stop: Cease or narrow when probable factual basis is not established.

actions.owner: Relevant governments and industry consortia
actions.ask: Coordinate lawful supply-chain standards with humanitarian exceptions and appeal routes.
actions.mechanism: Reduce recurring diversion while maintaining essential civilian supply.
actions.gate: Privacy, competition, international legal review.
actions.measure: Verified repeat-diversion incidence and civilian burden.
actions.stop: Reassess if overblocking exceeds benefits.

actions.owner: Diplomatic institutions, affected states, independent monitors
actions.ask: Support verified de-escalation frameworks tied to civilian protection and Ukraine’s sovereign consent.
actions.mechanism: Make agreements more credible and less vulnerable to renewed aggression.
actions.gate: International law, consent and enforceable monitoring.
actions.measure: Independently verified incident trends, humanitarian access and POW/missing-person progress.
actions.stop: Pause concessions if material compliance breaches go unaddressed.

cases.name: OHCHR August 2026 civilian casualty finding
cases.fact: At least 372 killed and 2,349 injured during August 2026. January–August totals: 2,222 killed and 13,058 injured.
cases.disposition: UN verification methodology supports documented minimum, not exhaustive battlefield totals.
cases.gap: Check whether September reporting has been published; avoid treating August as October live data.

cases.name: October 8 UN High Commissioner statement
cases.fact: UN human rights chief condemned civilian deaths and major power disruptions after reported strikes; noted concern over civilian casualties in occupied territory and Russia.
cases.disposition: Statement reports figures attributed to local authorities; not a replacement for independently verified monthly casualty database.
cases.gap: Follow the next OHCHR methodology-based publication.

cases.name: Ukraine 2026 humanitarian needs and response
cases.fact: UN estimates 10.8 million need humanitarian assistance, seeks $2.3bn to reach 4.1 million highly vulnerable people.
cases.disposition: A funding appeal and target, not a claim that all funding has arrived or people have been reached.
cases.gap: Retrieve contemporary funding and reach dashboards before measuring execution.

cases.name: 2026–27 winter readiness plan
cases.fact: Winter plan seeks $358.4m to support 2.1 million people from October 2026–March 2027.
cases.disposition: Plan targets heating, repairs, health, protection, food and cash assistance; donor funding is not assumed.
cases.gap: Obtain updated funding and distribution figures.

cases.name: October 2026 proposed energy ceasefire
cases.fact: US energy ceasefire publicly claimed; Russia and Ukraine did not confirm an independently verifiable implemented agreement on equal terms.
cases.disposition: Reported subsequent strikes should not automatically be styled a violation of a signed agreement whose terms are not evidenced.
cases.gap: Need authenticated bilateral scope, clock, independent observers, incident rubric and neutral case adjudication.

cases.name: Historical OSCE civilian monitoring
cases.fact: OSCE SMM discontinued operations on March 31, 2022; OSCE is not a UN organ.
cases.disposition: Past monitoring models offer lessons, not evidence that a mission exists today.
cases.gap: New monitoring proposal would require fresh authority, consent and security guarantees.
